title: CTF Cup / forensics,mobile,reverse / Mobile Treasure Hunters
goal:
Реши CTF-задачу "Mobile Treasure Hunters" (id=mobile-forensics, категория/теги: forensics,mobile,reverse, тип: static).
Нужен флаг формата ctfcup{...}. Найди флаг и выведи его.

=== Условие задачи ===
Изъят телефон курьера. Переписка велась в мессенджере **Burnt Note**, где сообщения самоуничтожаются после прочтения. После «тотальной чистки» таблица сообщений пуста, а синхронизация с сервером недоступна. Восстановите последнее сообщение переписки и найдите в нём контрольную фразу с адресом финальной точки.

=== Рабочие материалы ===
Все файлы раздачи лежат в текущей рабочей папке (workspace). Если есть подпапка work/ — в ней ЧАСТИЧНЫЙ ПРОГРЕСС предыдущих попыток решения (скрипты, промежуточные артефакты, заметки): внимательно изучи его и ПРОДОЛЖАЙ с этого места, не начинай с нуля. Если есть details.md — это официальное условие.
Для реверса доступны MCP-инструменты IDA (idalib) и отладчик pwndbg; можно запускать gdb/pwntools через bash и WSL.

=== Как завершить ===
Когда флаг найден (или задача зашла в тупик), заверши прогон. В итоговом summary ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО выведи на отдельных строках блок:
HARNESS_VERDICT: SOLVED|NOT_SOLVED
FLAG: <точный флаг ctfcup{...} или ->
Проверь, что флаг соответствует формату ctfcup{...}.

=== ПРОДОЛЖЕНИЕ (next round) ===
Повторный запуск. В рабочей папке УЖЕ есть прогресс прошлых прогонов (скрипты/артефакты в work/ и в корне). НЕ начинай с нуля: изучи имеющиеся файлы и ПРОДОЛЖИ с того места, доведи решение до флага.

label: Find the exact key-derivation glue in the dex smali dump: who calls the crypto p

objective: Find the exact key-derivation glue in the dex smali dump: who calls the crypto primitives (PBKDF2/root-HMAC/msgkey-HMAC/GCM) and with what arguments (salt, android_id usage, id semantics, AAD choice msg vs legacy).
detail:
Workspace: ctf-runs/mobile-forensics/workspace. Read work/recon-notes.md and work/seed-fragments.md for background (previous rounds). The full dex dump is work/dex-out/classes_smali.txt (~11k lines, custom dump format, one line per instruction). The dad-decompiled classes in work/dex-out/decompiled/ cover 9 classes but the ORCHESTRATION (glue) that calls the crypto primitives was not found in them — it may be a method the decompiler dropped or calls hidden in a class you haven't fully read.

Crypto primitives in class p9dd4e461.p0cc175b9 (see decompiled/p9dd4e461_p0cc175b9.java):
- m8277e091(pw, salt): PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256, 100000 iters, 256-bit
- m2510c390(): returns ASCII bytes of 'burnt-note/archive'
- m2db95e8e(key): HMAC-SHA256(key, 'burnt-note/root')
- m7b8b965a(base, nonce, id): HMAC-SHA256(base, nonce + '|burnt-note/step|' + id)
- m363b122c(key, nonce, id, ct): AES-GCM decrypt, AAD='burnt-note/msg/'+id (m0cc175b9), tag 128 bit
- m6f8f5771: encrypt counterpart
- mb2f5ff47(int): returns ASCII 'burnt-note/legacy/'+id — purpose unclear, possibly AAD for legacy frames
- m4a8a08f0(Iterable): '-'.join of fragment values
- p8277e091.m0cc175b9(Context): reads Settings.Secure android_id — WHO calls it and for WHAT (password? salt? not used?)

TASK: scan the whole classes_smali.txt (read it in chunks; the environment grep tool is broken, use python one-liners via bash if allowed, e.g. `python -c` to search lines containing 'm8277e091' / 'm2db95e8e' / 'm7b8b965a' / 'm6f8f5771' / 'm363b122c' / 'm2510c390' / 'mb2f5ff47' / 'm0cc175b9' / 'm4a8a08f0' / 'android_id' / 'getString' etc. and print line numbers plus surrounding context). Reconstruct the exact call graph and glue wiring. Also list ALL classes and ALL methods present in the smali dump and diff against the 9 decompiled files to find anything the decompiler dropped. Pay special attention to: (1) what string/id is passed as the `id` argument (row id? sequence? created_at?), (2) which AAD function is used for message frames (m0cc175b9 'burnt-note/msg/' vs mb2f5ff47 'burnt-note/legacy/'), (3) whether android_id '426079c78484367a' feeds the PBKDF2 salt or password, (4) whether the msgkey base is master or root, (5) any extra HMAC level between root and msgkey.

Write findings to work/glue_analysis.md with: exact wiring as pseudocode, evidence (smali line numbers), and confidence. If the glue genuinely does not exist in the APK (only the UI activity), say so explicitly and list what remains ambiguous. Keep it factual.

label: Offline brute-force the remaining key-derivation wiring combos against the row-1

objective: Offline brute-force the remaining key-derivation wiring combos against the row-1 GCM tag oracle; on a hit, decrypt all 10 message frames and extract the flag ctfcup{...}.
detail:
Workspace: ctf-runs/mobile-forensics/workspace. Prior rounds established (see work/recon-notes.md, work/dex-out/burntnote_decrypt.py, work/dex-out/decryption_result.json):
- 4 seed fragments (verified): 5a1b2ef44061 (whatsapp, ts 1768320131000), 64574c90358d (EXIF UserComment, ts 1768321441000), 3d91968bd7ed (diagnostics.log entropy, ts 1768321862011), ae4fa6e83015 (chrome paste URL, ts 1768322733000). App sorts fragments by timestamp ascending and joins with '-': password = '5a1b2ef44061-64574c90358d-3d91968bd7ed-ae4fa6e83015'.
- Crypto primitives (from decompiled p9dd4e461_p0cc175b9): master = PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256(pw, salt, 100000, 32); root = HMAC-SHA256(master, 'burnt-note/root'); msgkey = HMAC-SHA256(base, nonce + '|burnt-note/step|' + id); AES-256-GCM decrypt, GCMParameterSpec(128, nonce); AAD 'burnt-note/msg/'+id; frames are 1416B = 1400B zero-padded plaintext ct + 16B tag (tag at END).
- The primary hypothesis (salt='burnt-note/archive', base=root, id=rowid, AAD='burnt-note/msg/'+rowid) FAILS on all rows — see decryption_result.json. bruteforce_chain.py and bruteforce_stage2.py exist in work/dex-out/ but there is no record they were run to completion; you may re-run/extend them.

ORACLE: live row 1 of messages.db (id=1, nonce aa5cedeb3c5cddd95993c25b). Load frames ONLY via sqlite URI 'file:...?immutable=1' (opening normally DESTROYS the WAL; pristine copy in work/scratch/). Live rows: work/data/data/com.ctf.burntnote/databases/messages.db; WAL-recovered deleted rows: work/recovered_frames/rowid*.bin (first 12 bytes = nonce, rest = frame).

TASK: write work/brute_matrix.py that systematically tries the COMBINATIONS NOT yet covered, verifying each against the row-1 GCM tag (cheap check), and decrypting all 10 frames on a hit:
1. passwords: all 24 permutations of the 4 fragments joined '-' (ts-sorted first); plus variants: joined without separator, joined with '|', android_id '426079c78484367a' alone, alias 'b-note-77' alone.
2. salts: 'burnt-note/archive', android_id '426079c78484367a', 'b-note-77', '' (empty), 'burnt-note/root'.
3. msgkey base: master, root, and HMAC(root, 'burnt-note/step|'+id) style intermediates.
4. key shapes: base directly; HMAC(base, nonce+'|burnt-note/step|'+id); HMAC(base, '|burnt-note/step|'+id); HMAC(base, nonce); HMAC(base, nonce+'burnt-note/msg/'+id); HMAC(base, 'burnt-note/legacy/'+id); HMAC(base, nonce+'burnt-note/legacy/'+id).
5. id candidates: rowid (1), 0, 1, created_at 1768326600000, created_at//1000, and ALSO the message sequence position (for row 1 these coincide — additionally verify any hit against row id=3 whose seq is 2, to disambiguate; treat id as 'seq' meaning position among all 12 messages 1..12).
6. AADs: 'burnt-note/msg/'+id, 'burnt-note/legacy/'+id, '', nonce+'|burnt-note/step|'+id, 'burnt-note/step|'+id.
7. tag split: tag = frame[-16:] (primary) and tag = frame[:16] (fallback).
Use hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac (fast C). Memoize PBKDF2 per (pw,salt). Print every HIT with full combo details. On a hit: decrypt ALL rows (5 live + 5 WAL), rstrip(b'\x00'), decode utf-8, print all plaintexts, and search for the flag pattern ctfcup{...} and any 'контрольная фраза'/address. Save results to work/brute_matrix_result.json including the winning wiring and all plaintexts. Also update work/decrypt_status.md with what was tried (even if no hit — the negative result matrix is valuable). Do not run unbounded PBKDF2 counts beyond the listed combos (~120 combos max).
